root_cause.text: In `cgw_csum_crc8_rel()`, the loop and the final write use the raw unvalidated `s8` fields (`crc8->from_idx`, `crc8->to_idx`, `crc8->result_idx`) as array indices instead of the bounds-safe computed variables (`from`, `to`, `res`), causing out-of-bounds heap access when these fields contain negative values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the loop from `for (i = crc8->from_idx; ...)` to `for (i = from; ...)` and changes `cf->data[crc8->result_idx]` to `cf->data[res]`. The CVE description explicitly states that the loop and result write use raw s8 fields directly instead of the computed variables, and that with `from_idx = -64` on a 64-byte frame, `calc_idx()` returns 0 (passing the guard) but the loop iterates with `i = -64`, reading out-of-bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix CRC8 checksum calculation loop to iterate over the provided from and to indices instead of the fixed configuration indices.
intent_record.what: Changed loop boundaries in cgw_csum_crc8_rel from using crc8->from_idx/crc8->to_idx to using the passed parameters from and to.
intent_record.how: The loops now iterate over the actual range specified by the from and to function arguments instead of the fixed indices stored in the crc8 configuration structure, correcting the checksum computation to use the intended data range.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix CRC8 result index assignment to use the computed local variable `res` instead of the struct field `crc8->result_idx`, ensuring the CRC checksum is stored at the correct position for CAN FD frames.
intent_record.what: Replaced the array index from `crc8->result_idx` to `res` in the assignment `cf->data[...] = crc ^ crc8->final_xor_val;` within the function `cgw_csum_crc8_rel`.
intent_record.how: The change uses the locally computed variable `res` as the index for storing the CRC result instead of the struct field `crc8->result_idx`. This ensures the CRC is written to the correct byte position, which may differ for CAN FD frames or other configurations, fixing potential misplacement of the checksum.
